title: Mo and the Red Kite
learning_objectives: Answer a who/what question from the text
parent_prompts: Before reading: What do you think Mo will do with the kite?
After page 3: Why did the kite go up? What helped it?
After reading: Tell me the story in your own words. What happened first?

pages.image_alt: Mo, a small round bird, holds the string of a red kite that rests on the grass.

vocabulary.definition: A light toy you fly in the wind on a string.
vocabulary.example: The kite went up in the wind.

pages.text: The wind is still. The kite sits.
pages.image_alt: The kite lies flat on the grass. Mo looks at the sky.
pages.audio_script: The wind is still. The kite sits.

pages.text: Then the wind blows. Up goes the kite!
pages.image_alt: Lines show wind. The red kite rises high over Mo.
pages.audio_script: Then the wind blows. Up goes the kite!

pages.text: Mo runs. The kite runs too.
pages.image_alt: Mo runs across the grass with the kite flying behind.
pages.audio_script: Mo runs. The kite runs too.

pages.text: The sun goes down. Mo takes the kite home.
pages.image_alt: An orange sun sits low. Mo walks home holding the kite.
pages.audio_script: The sun goes down. Mo takes the kite home.

quiz.explanation: Page 1 says: Mo has a red kite.

quiz.prompt: Why does the kite go up?
quiz.explanation: On page 2 the wind is still and the kite sits. On page 3 the wind blows and the kite goes up.
The last page says the sun goes down and Mo takes the kite home.

quiz.prompt: Tell the story to a grown-up. What happened first, next, and last?
quiz.rubric: not yet: names one picture only; with support: two events with prompting; independent: three events in order in own words
quiz.explanation: A retell in order shows the child followed the story, not just the pictures.

items.text: The wind blows and the kite goes up.

prompts: What would you do if the wind stopped?
Where do you think Mo lives?

off_screen_prompt: Draw the kite going up. Tell someone what made it fly.
